source.headline: Iranian Media: Tehran Demands New Conditions From Washington To Resume Negotiations

US2Y.source: Trading Economics current US 2Y quote observed at prediction time

learning_profile.reason: Relevant GEOPOLITICS and context-aware segments were WATCH_ONLY/EARLY_SIGNAL rather than ACTIONABLE for a material directional-confidence change; current facts and pre-prediction context therefore dominate.

predictions.mechanism: New Iranian conditions reduce the probability of a rapid US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough, preserving geopolitical and energy risk premia that are supportive for gold, while a softer DXY provides an additional near-term tailwind.
predictions.invalidation: A confirmed agreement to restart talks without material preconditions, a ceasefire signal, or a sharp fall in oil risk premia would weaken the upside case.

predictions.mechanism: A harder path back to US-Iran talks extends the probability of high energy prices; Europe and German cyclicals are comparatively sensitive to renewed energy-cost and geopolitical pressure.
predictions.invalidation: Concrete diplomatic progress or a material drop in Brent would neutralize the downside bias.

predictions.mechanism: Persistent negotiation friction keeps the regional conflict and near-$100 Brent risk premium alive, mildly weighing on European risk assets.
predictions.invalidation: Verified de-escalation and falling oil prices would remove the principal bearish channel.

predictions.mechanism: Less immediate diplomatic progress sustains oil-driven inflation risk and already-elevated Treasury yields, creating a mild risk-off headwind for US equities.
predictions.invalidation: A diplomatic breakthrough or simultaneous decline in crude and Treasury yields would negate the mild downside signal.

predictions.mechanism: Persistent geopolitical and energy inflation risk can keep long yields elevated, which is a modest valuation headwind for duration-sensitive growth stocks despite the softer dollar.
predictions.invalidation: A clear fall in US10Y alongside diplomatic de-escalation would neutralize the downside bias.
